name: Ammannia

project_scope.selection_mode: two manifest-backed Central Texas learner species; recovered missing genus module
project_scope.sheet_source: Master Plant Pool rows 52–53; Genus Study Index row 201
project_scope.native_range_note: Both installed species currently retain UNRESOLVED project target-range status in species.json; no new native certification or metrics changes.

look_here_first: At a wetland plant's upper stem, find a pair of opposite, stalkless leaves with small ear-like lobes at the base. Follow the leaf axil to its flower cluster. Compare how far the cluster is stalked, count flowers, and measure a mature capsule with a millimeter scale; flower color alone will not settle the species.

shared_genus_traits.habit: Annual wet-ground herbs with branching, often four-angled stems.
shared_genus_traits.leaves: Opposite, simple, mostly entire, sessile leaves; bases often cordate/auriculate and clasping.
shared_genus_traits.flowers: Small flowers in leaf-axil cymes, generally four-parted; persistent cup-shaped floral tube (hypanthium) with sepals and sometimes tiny accessory teeth.
shared_genus_traits.fruit: Many-seeded, rounded capsule associated with a persistent floral tube.
shared_genus_traits.family_bridge: The ovary is superior, sitting within—not fused below—the floral tube. The family lesson compares this with Onagraceae.

species_comparison_matrix.plain: Stalk between leaf axil and first branch of flower cluster
species_comparison_matrix.Ammannia auriculata: Often slender, typically about 3–9 mm in published flora descriptions; can vary.
species_comparison_matrix.Ammannia coccinea: Usually very short, stout or apparently absent, but descriptions allow 0–9 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Strongest when combined with cluster compactness and mature capsule size; stalk-length ranges overlap.

species_comparison_matrix.plain: Count distinct flowers or fruit stalks at one node
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Counts overlap; check multiple intact nodes.

species_comparison_matrix.plain: Measure widest width of ripe rounded fruit
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Useful tie-breaker at full maturity; boundary overlaps near 3.5 mm and immature fruit is misleading.

species_comparison_matrix.plain: Measure the flower cup, not its stalk
species_comparison_matrix.Ammannia coccinea: Often around 2–3.5 mm in North American descriptions; literature sometimes gives 3–5 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Confirm mature flowers under magnification; measurement and regional treatments vary.

species_comparison_matrix.plain: Look for the little ear-shaped lobes where opposite leaves clasp the stem
species_comparison_matrix.interpretation: Shared genus clue, NOT a dependable species split; useful against Rotala ramosior.

quick_key.if: Opposite clasping leaves; loose, clearly stalked cymes with many small flowers; mature capsule commonly <3.5 mm
quick_key.then: Check Ammannia auriculata; verify floral tube and several fruiting nodes.

quick_key.if: Opposite clasping leaves; tight few-flowered clusters on short stout stalks; mature capsule commonly >3.5 mm
quick_key.then: Check Ammannia coccinea; confirm with fruit and flowers.
Leave Ammannia sp. until fruiting; the two species overlap.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Opposite leaf bases → axillary cluster stalk → mature capsule → floral tube/calyx.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Little rounded ears where a leaf clasps the stem
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: At a middle or upper pair of opposite leaves; photograph both bases in profile.
shared_structure_examples.why: Supports Ammannia against tapered-base Rotala; does not alone separate the two Ammannia species.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: paired node/leaf-base macro with mm scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: Flower cluster in the angle between leaf and stem, and the stalk holding that cluster
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Measure from leaf axil to first branch of cluster, not to an individual flower.
shared_structure_examples.why: Relative stalk thickness, length and flower count are practical species clues.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: same-scale side-by-side mature axillary clusters of both species

shared_structure_examples.plain: Little persistent flower cup with sepal points
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Side of an intact flower; compare cup ribs and the true sepal teeth with any accessory projections.
shared_structure_examples.why: Confirms the Lythraceae/Ammannia floral structure; flower petals are short-lived.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: 10×–20× flower-side macro or dissected flower with ruler

shared_structure_examples.plain: Rounded seed pod remaining inside the old flower cup
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Mature fruit at several nodes; measure its widest diameter.
shared_structure_examples.why: Capsule diameter is a stronger species separator than flower color.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched mature fruit/calyx macros, mm ruler, optional cutaway

priority: Confirm genus from opposite sessile auriculate leaves and axillary flowers.
Find several mature axillary clusters and measure peduncle length.
Count flowers/fruit per cluster and measure fully ripe capsules.
Use floral tube and calyx details to confirm; preserve Ammannia sp. for ambiguous plants.
overlap_cautions: Both species can have ear-shaped leaf bases and pink-purple flowers; neither is a unique species diagnostic.
Published peduncle lengths and cluster counts overlap; do not turn a tendency into an absolute key.
Capsule measurements require fully mature fruit and a visible millimeter scale.
Ammannia robusta can be similar; include it as a regional look-alike, not an installed project species.
Source-pool inclusion and native-range status are separate; both species remain range-unresolved in canonical metadata.

comparison_cards.title: Loose stalked cymes versus tight clusters
comparison_cards.look_here_first: At several upper leaf axils, compare length/thickness of cluster stalk and flower count.
photo_requirements: paired axillary cyme macros with ruler
comparison_cards.caution: A. coccinea stalk length is variable; confirm with ripe fruit.

comparison_cards.title: Small versus larger mature capsules
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure the widest diameter of several mature capsules: often 1.5–3.5 mm versus 3.5–5 mm.
photo_requirements: mature capsule side views with millimeter ruler
comparison_cards.caution: Measurements meet around 3.5 mm; immature capsules cannot be keyed confidently.

comparison_cards.title: Ammannia versus Rotala and other redstems
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare auriculate leaf bases and cymes with Rotala ramosior's tapered leaf bases and tiny usually solitary axillary flowers; A. robusta needs floral and capsule confirmation.
photo_requirements: Ammannia versus Rotala matched leaf-base macros
flower/capsule side views of A. robusta if legally available
comparison_cards.caution: Rotala and A. robusta are look-alikes, not extra canonical Ammannia species in this two-species lesson.

local_lookalikes.name: Rotala ramosior
local_lookalikes.distinction: Opposite leaves usually taper toward the base rather than forming obvious clasping ears; flowers tiny and often solitary at axils; verify floral tube.

local_lookalikes.name: Ammannia robusta
local_lookalikes.distinction: A related redstem with overlapping vegetative appearance; use a current regional key, flower cluster and mature capsule characters; not one of the two canonical project Ammannia species.

local_lookalikes.name: Lythrum spp.
local_lookalikes.distinction: More conspicuous flowers on elongate axes and different floral-tube/leaf-base combination; see Lythrum genus lesson.
